headline: Samsung is reportedly developing three versions of its zNAND flash storage for AI, aimed at on-device AI, data centres and AI inference.
score_reason: Kept at 5: read in full via BigGo and properly hedged, but it is an early-stage plan from unnamed sources that Samsung has not announced.
importance_line: Buyers of AI servers and devices could eventually get flash storage built for specific AI jobs, but the products are at an early stage, Samsung has not confirmed them, and no specifications or launch dates are known.
summary: BigGo Finance reports, citing industry sources, that Samsung Electronics is in early development of three zNAND flash-memory products for AI: zNAND-O for AI running on devices, zNAND-T for data centres and zNAND-I for AI inference, the stage where a trained model answers requests, after showing a zNAND-O mock-up at the FMS 2026 memory event in August. Samsung has made no official announcement, and the report says SK Hynix, its South Korean rival, is following a similar path with its own three-product AIN family.
notes: The pool item (Sammy Fans) is behind a Cloudflare block; the same story was read on BigGo Finance, which does not name the original outlet, so the credit is 'BigGo Finance, citing industry sources' and the url is the BigGo page. Not carried in earlier editions.
